messages:
maya: Quick proposal — standardize quant profile packaging into a single 'qpack' artifact consumed by Redwood Optimize. Goal: one manifest, multiple variants (FP8/INT8/GPTQ/AWQ), clear accuracy deltas, and recommended deployment profiles. Sketch below.

ben: +1 on standardizing. quick q: why 'qpack' vs keeping qprof naming? just to avoid confusion with old manifests?

maya: exactly. qpack = bundle of profiles + eval metadata + deploy hints. keeps legacy qprof as a compatibility alias but new tooling expects qpack.

li: can you show a sample manifest layout? helps to lock fields and types.

maya: sure — example manifest (human-readable snippet):

```json
{
  "format_version": "1.0",
  "qpack_version": "0.1.0",
  "model": "llama-3-13b",
  "model_hash": "sha256:abcd1234",
  "variants": [
    {
      "id": "awq-fp8-h100",
      "name": "fp8-awq",
      "backend": "awq",
      "quant_bits": 8,
      "hw_targets": ["h100","a100"],
      "accuracy_deltas": {"mmlu": "-0.35%", "perplexity": "+0.8%"},
      "eval_artifact": "gs://redwood-evals/llama3-13b/awq-fp8-2026-02-10.tgz",
      "recommended_deploy_profiles": ["latency-first", "mixed"],
      "notes": "good latency win on H100, small MMLU drop within threshold"
    },
    {
      "id": "gptq-int8-a100",
      "name": "int8-gptq",
      "backend": "gptq",
      "quant_bits": 8,
      "hw_targets": ["a100"],
      "accuracy_deltas": {"mmlu": "-0.92%", "rouge": "-0.5%"},
      "eval_artifact": "gs://redwood-evals/llama3-13b/gptq-int8-2026-02-10.tgz",
      "recommended_deploy_profiles": ["cost-savvy"],
      "notes": "best cost reduction, larger accuracy cost on reasoning tasks"
    }
  ],
  "optimize_recommendations": {
    "latency-first": {"batch": 1, "kv_cache": true, "prefill_parallel": false},
    "cost-savvy": {"batch": 8, "kv_cache": false}
  },
  "metadata": {"author": "maya", "created": "2026-02-10T14:12:00Z", "eval_seed": "42"}
}
```

sam: this looks good. couple of notes: 1) accuracy_deltas should always include per-task breakdown and absolute baseline numbers in eval artifact. 2) add a compatibility tag for runtime kernel assumptions (fused_gelu, stable_rng) so runtime can auto-choose kernels.

ben: +1. also recommend semantic versioning for qpack_version and a separate compatibility string for older runtimes: e.g. compat: "optimize>=2.3, runtime>=1.9"

maya: will add compat and per-task absolute scores. thinking about naming for artifact files: qpack-llama3-13b-v0.1.0+awq.h100.tar.gz — opinions?

li: that's fine. prefer using "+" to indicate variant metadata (hardware/backend). For machine-readable fields we also keep tags: ["awq","h100","latency"]

qpack-bot: uploaded qpack artifact to gs://redwood-qpacks/llama3-13b/qpack-0.1.0-awq-h100.tgz :white_check_mark: (size: 2.1GB)

sam: bakeoff summary (short): AWQ-FP8 (h100) -> latency -35%, cost -28%, MMLU -0.35pt. GPTQ-INT8 (a100) -> cost -48%, latency -20%, MMLU -0.92pt. include per-task CSV in eval_artifact.

ben: add a field in manifest: "release_impact": "regression-risk:low|requires-canary" or something similar so console can show rollout gating.

maya: good call. will add release_impact + rollout_hint (canary_percent, sla_target).

li: one operational consideration: runtime should validate hw_targets against available instance types and automatically fallback to next-best variant if hardware mismatch. manifest should include fallback_chain: ["awq-fp8-h100","gptq-int8-a100","fp16-hosted"]

maya: noted. final next steps: I'll draft PR with spec, example qpack, and a small reference implementation of the parser in python. @li please review packaging naming rules. @ben can you add Optimize UI hooks for showing accuracy deltas and deploy recommendations?

ben: yup I'll add a UI card for qpacks that surfaces accuracy_deltas and recommended_deploy_profiles, with a toggle to auto-apply Optimize suggestions.

sam: make sure to surface absolute eval counts and seeds in the UI so product teams can decide risk thresholds.

maya: thanks. I'll open PR today and link artifacts. :rocket:
